Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

DataEditR 2.0.0

Tabulator grid replaces rhandsontable

  • The data grid is now a thin htmlwidget around the MIT-licensed ‘Tabulator’ JavaScript library (6.7.1, bundled). rhandsontable is no longer a dependency, so the forked rhandsontable is no longer required and the CRAN version works as intended.
  • Edits are sent to R as cell-level changes (deltas) instead of whole tables. On a 100,000 row table an edit round trip takes ~50 ms and only the visible rows are rendered in the browser.
  • Rows and columns carry stable identifiers. Filtered rows and selected columns are views onto the full data, so edits apply directly to the master copy (no synchronisation step), and renaming a column no longer touches the data.
  • Undo and redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, or the toolbar buttons). A paste, fill or range clear is a single undo step.
  • Spreadsheet-style range selection, copy/paste, Delete to clear a range and Ctrl+D to fill down. Double-click a header to rename a column; right-click rows or headers to insert/delete rows and columns.
  • Pasting from Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice handles Windows line endings, the trailing line break and quoted cells with line breaks, adds rows when the block is longer than the table, converts formatted numbers (1,234.5, $12, 45%), d/m/y and m/d/y dates and yes/no, and asks once about values that do not fit their columns. Copying quotes cells with line breaks and copies an HTML table for spreadsheets.
  • New column types in col_options: "datetime", "time", "textarea", "url", "colour", "slider", "rating" and numbers within limits (c(min = 0, max = 10, step = 0.5)), alongside checkboxes, dropdowns, "date" and "password". Slider limits and rating stars are set with e.g. c(type = "slider", min = 0, max = 1, step = 0.05). Values that do not fit a column’s input are caught whether they are typed or pasted, and values already in the data that do not fit are marked.
  • Cells of templates and new columns that were never filled in are returned as NA (they were empty strings), like cells that were cleared.
  • Factor columns are returned as factors (ordered factors stay ordered) with their original levels, and new values are added as levels after them. Earlier versions returned them as text unless col_factor = TRUE, which now only converts character columns.
  • The generated code (code) starts from the data that was opened from the Open menu, returns matrices as matrices and new tables as data frames, and recreates factors with the same levels as the returned data.
  • Dates are only read from complete YYYY-MM-DD values (as.Date() read 15/03/2024 as the year 15); other formats are converted in the browser before they reach R.
  • col_options no longer disables adding or removing columns, and col_readonly columns are locked in the grid rather than reverted after editing.
  • A change counter is shown above the grid, and track now highlights cells with a tinted fill that is distinct from the range selection.
  • Column types are preserved: only empty template/new columns are passed through type.convert() on return, so character columns such as "001" are no longer converted to numbers. Dates stay dates, and matrices, tibbles and data.tables are returned with their original class.

Comments, drag to fill and a colour picker

  • Cells can carry comments: right-click a cell (or press Shift+F2) to add, edit or delete one. Commented cells get an amber corner, and the comment shows when the pointer rests on the cell and in the record form. Comments are kept in drafts and returned with the data as attr(x, "comments"), a data frame of the row, column, comment, user and time; data opened with that attribute shows its comments. Comments on database rows follow the rows when changes are committed or other rows are loaded.
  • Selections have a fill handle: drag the corner of a selection down, up or across to fill the cells it passes over. One value is copied; two or more numbers, dates (days or months apart, month ends stay month ends) or text ending in a number (Week 1, Week 2) carry on as a series, and anything else is repeated. Hold Ctrl to copy without a series. A fill is one undo step, and values that do not fit a column are asked about first, as for a paste.
  • A paste wider than the columns to the right of the selected cell adds columns (V1, V2, …) unless col_edit = FALSE; extra values were ignored.
  • Colour columns (col_options = list(x = "colour")) are edited with a colour picker: type a colour, pick a swatch (the colours already in the column, then R’s palette and the Okabe-Ito palette) or any colour with the browser’s picker. list(type = "colour", palette = c(...)) sets the swatches offered. R colour names such as "grey50" now show the right swatch (R’s "green" and "gray" are not the CSS ones), and values that are not colours get a dashed one.
  • The History tab lists earlier editing sessions of the same data, newest first and folded away: data_edit(log = "file.csv") reads them from its file, and dataEditServer(history = ) takes a data frame (or a reactive) of earlier log entries, for example read from a database table. The change log has a new session column (when the editing session started) to tell sessions apart; log files written before keep their columns.
  • The Code tab is much faster on big data: on 100,000 rows it takes about 0.6 s after column actions (was about 5 s) and 0.3 s after edits (was 1.5 s), with the same code.

Tables too big to load

  • Database tables no longer have to fit in memory: at most 100,000 rows are loaded at a time (db_table(limit = ), default getOption("DataEditR.db_rows", 100000); it was all rows). The header and a new Rows button in the toolbar show how many rows are loaded out of how many there are.
  • Rows loads other rows: those matching a filter written like dplyr::filter() (translated to SQL by dbplyr, limited to columns and the functions formulas may use), sorted by a column, at most a number of rows. The dialog counts the matching rows first, and unsaved changes are saved to the database or discarded before other rows are loaded.
  • Queries that cannot be written back (SQL, joins, tables without a primary key, e.g. Parquet files read by DuckDB) are opened read-only instead of failing; db_table(readonly = FALSE) still stops with an error, and readonly = TRUE opens any table read-only.

Labelled data (SPSS, Stata and SAS)

  • SPSS (.sav, .por), Stata (.dta) and SAS (.sas7bdat, .xpt) files are read with haven, from a file name or the Open menu (unless read_fun is given). save_as files ending in .sav, .dta or .xpt are written with haven, and the Export menu can download SPSS and Stata files.
  • Variable labels, value labels (haven_labelled, or the labels attribute of labelled/sjlabelled) and SPSS user-defined missing values are kept through every edit, added and removed rows, undo and column actions. Variable labels of plain columns were dropped when rows were added or removed, and text columns with value labels made the editor fail.
  • Cells show values with their labels and columns with value labels get an lbl badge. The cell editor lists the labels, and labels typed, pasted or entered in the record form are stored as their values. User-defined missing values are shown muted and count as missing in summaries and the “is missing” filter.
  • Labels… in the column menu changes the variable label and the value labels (one value = label per line), recorded as one step in the code. Change type turns labelled columns into factors or text with their labels (haven::as_factor()) or into plain values (haven::zap_labels()).
  • The generated code writes SPSS missing values as values (they were written as NA) and puts back variable labels that tibble::add_row() drops. Formulas may use haven::as_factor(), zap_labels(), zap_label(), labelled(), labelled_spss() and structure().

Column summaries and a record form

  • Each column header shows a summary of the column, worked out in R from all rows: a histogram of numbers and dates or the most common values, the share of missing values and the number of distinct values. Clicking a bar filters the rows (a range for numbers, a period for dates, a value for the rest), clicking the missing share shows the rows where the value is missing (a new “is missing” filter), and the number of distinct values opens the details (smallest, largest, mean, median, standard deviation). Summaries are kept up to date as you edit, only recomputing the columns that changed. A toolbar button hides them, and col_summary = FALSE leaves them out.
  • A new Record tab (and toolbar button) shows the selected row as a form, for entering or checking data one record at a time. Its fields use the column inputs and checks of the grid, show broken rules under the fields and move with the grid; New adds a row at the end.
  • Double-click a column’s name (rather than anywhere in its header) to rename it.

Column actions and validation rules

  • A column’s menu (the new ⋮ button in its header, or a right-click) has actions that change the whole column: Formula… (a new column or new values from an R expression such as round(mpg * 0.425, 1)), Find and replace…, Recode values…, Change type and sorting. Each shows a preview and is recorded as one dplyr verb (mutate(), arrange()), so the generated code says what was done rather than listing every changed value. The editor runs that same verb, so the code gives exactly the result, and checks this before showing it. Formulas can only use columns and common functions, so they are safe in shiny apps. Turn the actions off with col_actions = FALSE.
  • rules checks the data as it is edited: formulas that are TRUE for valid rows, named with their messages (e.g. "End is after the start" = ~ end >= start). Cells that break a rule are marked, a new Problems tab lists them, the status bar counts them and Done asks before returning data with problems. Columns can be made required or unique, given limits or a pattern, or a formula, from their menu (Rules…). dataEditProblems() returns the problems in shiny apps.
  • Code for columns inserted between other columns now puts them in place (mutate(..., .after = )).
  • The change log gains a code column with the verb of column actions.

Change log, notes and drafts

  • Every change is recorded with the time, the user and how it was made (typed, pasted, filled, cleared, undone, redone or reverted). The new History tab of the review panel lists the changes step by step, and each step can be given a note saying why it was made.
  • data_edit(log = "changes.csv") adds the change log to a csv file when Done is pressed (or passes it to a function), so one file can keep the history of many editing sessions.
  • Changes are saved as a draft while editing (autosave = TRUE). If the editor is closed without pressing Done or Cancel, opening the same data again offers to restore the changes with their history. Drafts are kept in tools::R_user_dir("DataEditR", "data") and removed after 30 days.
  • Cancel asks before changes are thrown away.
  • In shiny apps, dataEditLog() returns the change log, dataEditCommit() returns the log of the changes it saved, and dataEditServer() gains autosave and user arguments.

New editor layout

  • One toolbar replaces the old input row, icon buttons and undo/redo line: Open, Undo/Redo, Columns, filter chips, Find in data, Review changes, Code, Export and a keyboard shortcuts sheet (press ?).
  • Filter rows by typing in the boxes under each column header: min/max for numbers, a multi-select list for columns with few distinct values and “contains” for text. Active filters appear as chips in the toolbar. This replaces the filter dialog inside data_edit() (the dataFilter module is still exported).
  • Show or hide columns from the Columns menu (or a column’s right-click menu), replacing the column selection dialog inside data_edit() (the dataSelect module is still exported).
  • Review panel: lists every edited, added, removed or renamed cell, row and column with a button to revert it (reverts can be undone), plus “Revert all”, and a Code tab that shows the data_code() output as you edit.
  • Status bar: rows and columns on screen, Excel-style sum/mean/count of the selected cells, and a summary of changes.
  • Typing text into a number or date column asks whether to store NA, convert the column to text or cancel, instead of silently converting the column. "NA" is treated as a missing value in typed columns.
  • “+ Add row” under the grid and a “+” header to add a column; headers show type badges and a lock on read-only columns; Ctrl+F finds values.
  • The Done button gains a menu to return all data or only what is on screen (replacing the scissors toggle) and, with save_as, whether to save.
  • Open (R object, file upload or new table) and Export (all data or what is on screen) menus replace the dataInput/dataOutput row; both modules are still exported.
  • Bootstrap 5 theme by default (theme = NULL); Bootswatch names such as "yeti" now select the Bootstrap 5 version. shinyBS and miniUI are no longer dependencies.
  • Two more Tabulator 6.7.1 hot spots are patched (row display checks and range re-layout touched every row), keeping edits at ~35 ms on 100,000 rows.

Database tables

  • data_edit() and dataEditServer() accept dbplyr lazy tables (e.g. data_edit(tbl(con, "artists")), optionally filtered), or a db_table(). Rows are matched by primary key (detected for SQLite, DuckDB and PostgreSQL), edits are staged until Done, the user confirms a summary, and changes are written in a single transaction with optimistic concurrency checks (the commit is rolled back if any row changed in the database since it was loaded). Columns that are not part of the table are read-only and schema changes are disabled.
  • code = TRUE generates rows_update(), rows_append() and rows_delete() code for database edits.
  • New dataEditCommit() saves the changes made in a dataEditServer() editor, so shiny applications can write database edits (in a single transaction, rolled back with an editr_conflict error if rows changed in the meantime) and read the rows back with the keys the database generated. For other data the current data becomes the new starting point for the review panel and change tracking. dataEditChanges() returns a summary of the changes that have not been saved yet.
  • data_edit() returns database rows as read back after the commit, so new rows include their generated keys.

Other changes

  • data_code() now inserts added rows at their edited positions using tibble::add_row(.before = ), so the generated code reproduces row order.
  • dataFilterServer() and dataSelectServer() gain a reset argument so filters are kept while data is edited; dataSelectServer() also returns the selected column names.
  • Fix dataFilter filters being re-created by stale observers after “Remove Filters”.
  • A filter that matches no rows now shows an empty table rather than all rows.
  • row_bind adds typed empty rows, so numeric columns stay numeric.
  • dataEditServer() gains rows and columns arguments to display a subset of the data; row_index is no longer needed.
  • dataEditServer() applies rows and columns when the data is first loaded (and when it is reloaded), not only when they change.
  • Matrices without row names are returned without row names.
  • dataInputServer() can load an uploaded file after an R object, and no longer fails on data without columns.
  • dataOutputServer() no longer loops when the first column holds row names.
  • dataFilterServer() has been simplified: filters without levels are ignored, “between” accepts its limits in any order, and “not between” or “not contain” filters that match every row return no rows.
  • col_bind lists without names get unique column names (V1, V2, …).
  • Database tables built from raw SQL queries give a clear error asking for db_table(x, table = , key = ), and factor values are written as text.
  • The table behind a lazy table is found with dbplyr 2.3, 2.4 and 2.5 (which stores quoted table paths such as `main`.`cars`).
  • The RStudio add-in returns the highlighted data when cancelled and accepts any object with dimensions or a database table.
  • Test suite covers the gadget, the shiny modules (with shiny::testServer()) and the database backend, with over 95% code coverage.
  • Documentation: new pkgdown articles on editing database tables, using the modules in shiny apps and what is new in 2.0, a rewritten user guide with new screenshots, and a new logo with the package name typed into a table.

DataEditR 1.0.0

Major New Features

  • Add change tracking with the new track parameter in data_edit() and dataEditServer(). Set track = TRUE to highlight edited and added cells with a blue border, or pass a CSS color string (e.g. track = "red") for a custom highlight colour. Uses Handsontable’s afterRenderer hook and name-based cell matching so that inserted rows or columns no longer cause all subsequent cells to appear changed.
  • Add tidyverse-style code generation via the new data_code() function and updated code argument in data_edit(). Instead of dput() output, the editor now generates human-readable dplyr pipe code using rename(), select(), mutate(), slice(), and tibble::add_row() to replicate column renames, additions/removals, cell value changes, and row additions/removals. Row names (e.g. those in mtcars) are preserved via tibble::rownames_to_column() / tibble::column_to_rownames().

Automatic Data Synchronisation

  • Remove the sync button in favour of automatic data synchronisation. Changes made to filtered or selected data subsets are now automatically merged back into the master copy of the data as they are made.
  • Fix bug where column indices were not passed to the sync logic (values$cols instead of values$columns).
  • Add auto parameter to dataSyncServer() to allow automatic synchronisation when used as a standalone module.
  • Improve performance by preventing unnecessary table re-renders after data synchronisation. Filter and select modules no longer reset on every sync.

Bug Fixes

  • Fix factor column crash: passing a data frame with factor columns no longer causes an error in hot_context_menu. Factor columns are now converted to character before rendering and converted back on output via col_factor.
  • Fix dataFilter “not between” and “not contain” filter logic which incorrectly used ncol() instead of nrow(), causing wrong row indices to be returned.
  • Fix dataFilter multi-filter intersection which used duplicated() and missed rows matching all filters when no duplicates existed. Now uses table() to correctly compute the intersection.
  • Fix stale input$x race condition in dataEditServer() when switching reactive data. A data_loading flag now prevents the old table’s input$x from overwriting values$x before the new data has rendered.

DataEditR 0.1.7

  • Remove the sync button in favour of automatic data synchronisation. Changes made to filtered or selected data subsets are now automatically merged back into the master copy of the data as they are made.
  • Fix bug where column indices were not passed to the sync logic (values$cols instead of values$columns).
  • Add auto parameter to dataSyncServer() to allow automatic synchronisation when used as a standalone module.
  • Improve performance by preventing unnecessary table re-renders after data synchronisation. Filter and select modules no longer reset on every sync.

DataEditR 0.1.6

  • Update FontAwesome icon names.

DataEditR 0.1.5

  • Add cancel argument to data_edit() to allow control over return value when the data editor is deliberately closed by the user, set to the original input dat by default.
  • Make the switch to bslib for more flexibility in setting custom themes data_edit(). Users can now supply a bs_theme object to the theme argument to fully customise the appearance of the data_edit() UI.
  • Fix handling of numeric row names to ensure maintenance of row indices relative to the master copy.
  • Improved handling of highlighted data_edit() calls within RStudio.

DataEditR 0.1.4

  • Fix header location on scroll.
  • Make sure column names are retained when loading empty datasets within dataInput.
  • Add checks for empty data within dataInput and dataEdit to ensure that the supplied data always contains as least a single row and column.
  • Add support for writing data to googlesheets by calling write_fun as the application closes.
  • Fix data_edit() to ensure that we don’t search for data through RStudio addin if RStudio is not in use.

DataEditR 0.1.3

  • Display hints when user hovers cursor over buttons.
  • Make sure R objects containing . can be loaded into the data editor.
  • Turn on highlighting for columns and rows.
  • Add dataSync module to handle synchronisation of an edited data subset with the complete dataset.
  • Improved support for tibbles.
  • Fix dataFilter to ensure the logic and levels are always updated when the column selection changes.

DataEditR 0.1.2

  • data_edit() can now export the code required to generate the final edited version of the data to an R script.
  • Update vignette and website to demonstrate usage of code argument.
  • Make sure to search the correct environment when creating templates or reading files.

DataEditR 0.1.1

  • Ensure dataInput searches for data outside data_edit().
  • Prevent loading of highlighted data object in RStudio when data has been supplied to data_edit() directly.
  • Allow saving by write_fun whenever save_as is supplied.

DataEditR 0.1.0

  • Make the switch to GitHub Actions for continuous integration.
  • Update dataSelect and dataFilter examples now that the return values are lists instead of reactive expressions.

DataEditR 0.0.9

  • Minor improvements to ensure that the original data is retained when new columns are added or renamed. Requires installation of rhandsontable from install_github("DillonHammill/rhandsontable").

DataEditR 0.0.8

  • Add dataSelect and dataFilter modules to filter data,
  • Add a Sync button to update the entire dataset with changes made to a subset. Data is still exported as a whole but a new button could be added in the future to export the subsetted data.
  • Add cut button to allow return of subsetted data upon closing the application with the Done button.

DataEditR 0.0.7

  • Create dataInput, dataEdit and dataOutput modules.
  • Create RStudio addin to interactively edit data.
  • Update user interface to allow interactive file selection or input of R data objects.
  • Add new viewer options to open the data editor in a dialog box, browser or RStudio viewer pane. This can be controlled through the viewer argument and has been set to use a dialog box by default. Additional arguments viewer_height and viewer_width have been added to allow control over the dimensions of dialog boxes.
  • Add a cancel button in top left to return data unchanged.
  • Add new hide argument to optionally display the dataInput and dataOutput modules. This functionality requires the shinyjs package. The hide argument allows users to maximize the space available to display the data and also prevent users from interacting with these modules. It is still possible to save data to file when dataOutput module is not visible, by simply supplying the file name to the save_as argument of data_edit().
  • Improve handling of row names with the dataEdit module.
  • Add helper function to handle generation of templates based on inputs to data_edit() to make it easier to create data.frames from scratch. The default template size has been increased to be a 10 x 10 grid.
  • Add logo_side argument to control whether the logo should be placed on the left or right of the title.
  • Add new code argument to data_edit() to print the code required to create the edited data to the console.

DataEditR 0.0.6

  • Add ability to pass column names to data_edit() to construct a template data.frame with pre-defined column names.

DataEditR 0.0.5

  • Fix row indices when rows are added or removed.
  • Improve handling of duplicate row indices in case of accidental editing.

DataEditR 0.0.4

  • Add col_readonly argument to prevent users from editing values or column names of certain columns.
  • Prevent error when column is clicked but not edited.

DataEditR 0.0.3

  • Add col_names argument to allow control over which column names can be edited by the user.

DataEditR 0.0.2

  • Fixes for CRAN submission.

DataEditR 0.0.1

  • Add data_edit() to allow interactive data viewing, entry and editing.
